title: Tool modes move into a flyout on the tool button, so the tool bar stops growing
goal: Picking the Measure tool currently adds six controls to the tool bar: four labelled mode chips, a Snap menu and a Show menu. The bar is a fixed strip that has to survive a narrow window, and every future tool with modes would spread the same way. Modes should live in the tool button itself, opening upward out of the bar the way a pro editor does it, so selecting a tool never changes how wide the bar is.
notes: Playtest 2026-08-23: horizontal space in the toolbar is scarce and the measure options row is eating it. Reference behaviour is the Photoshop tool flyout. Current code: EditorView.measureOptions builds the chip row plus measureSnapOption and measureShowOption, gated by hasMeasureOptions; contextualToolOptions is where per-tool rows are added, so wand and crop options are the same pattern and should follow once measure proves it. The rule is written up as UX-PATTERNS D15, including the mode-versus-setting test: if it changes what the pointer does it can be a mode, if it changes how the result looks it is a setting. Build the flyout as a shared control, not a measure-only one, since shape, marquee and brush all need it next.
acceptance: Selecting any tool leaves the tool bar exactly the same width, measured before and after
The Measure tool button shows the active mode as a glyph, with a small marker saying it has more
Press and hold, or clicking the marker, opens a flyout above the bar listing the modes with names and shortcuts, closing on pick, Escape and outside click
Pressing the tool key again cycles modes without opening anything
Snap and Show leave the bar: they are settings, not modes, and live with the tool properties
A tool with only one mode shows no marker and no flyout
